tool.help:
**What it does**
Checks a text, integer or float value against a condition and returns ``true`` or ``false``. Use it in a workflow to turn a parameter, such as a selected option or a threshold, into a boolean that controls a ``when`` condition or feeds **Combine boolean parameters**.
The value to compare to can itself be connected, so you can also compare two workflow parameters with each other. If it is connected and turns out unset (null), the job fails.
**Text checks**
=================================== ======================================= ================================= Check True when the value ... Example that is true =================================== ======================================= ================================= is equal to is exactly the given text ``paired`` vs ``paired`` is not equal to differs from the given text ``paired`` vs ``single`` contains contains the given text ``hello world`` vs ``lo w`` does not contain does not contain the given text ``hello`` vs ``xyz`` starts with begins with the given text ``sample_01`` vs ``sample`` does not start with does not begin with the given text ``sample_01`` vs ``control`` ends with ends with the given text ``reads.fastq.gz`` vs ``.gz`` does not end with does not end with the given text ``reads.fastq.gz`` vs ``.bam`` matches a regular expression matches the regular expression ``sample_01`` vs ``^sample_\d+$`` does not match a regular expression does not match the regular expression ``paired`` vs ``^single`` is empty or unset is the empty text or unset (null) the empty text is not empty has at least one character ``a`` is unset (null) is unset; the empty text does not count an empty optional parameter is set (not null), even if empty has any value, including the empty text the empty text =================================== ======================================= =================================
Text checks are case-sensitive unless **Ignore case** is set. Regular expressions use JavaScript syntax and match anywhere in the value; anchor them with ``^`` and ``$`` to match the whole value. An invalid regular expression makes the job fail.
**Integer and float checks**
================================ =========================== Check Example that is true ================================ =========================== is equal to (==) 5 == 5 is not equal to (!=) 5 != 6 is less than (<) 4 < 5 is less than or equal to (<=) 5 <= 5 is greater than (>) 6 > 5 is greater than or equal to (>=) 5 >= 5 is unset (null) an empty optional parameter is set (not null) any value, including 0 ================================ ===========================
Floats are compared exactly: a value computed upstream as ``0.1 + 0.2`` is not equal to ``0.3``. For computed floats, prefer ``<`` or ``>`` over ``==``.
**Unset (null) values**
A value is unset when it comes from an optional workflow parameter that was left empty, or from a step that was skipped. The "is empty or unset", "is unset (null)" and "is set (not null)" checks handle unset values directly. For every other check the setting **If the value to check is unset (null)** decides the result:
- **Fail the job** (default): stop with an error. - **Result is false** / **Result is true**: return that result.
